title: Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan Sign Mecca Defence Pact, Spain-Italy Schengen Row Escalates, DRC Ebola Surpasses 4,000 Cases
subhead: Three major Muslim powers formalised a mutual defence agreement in Mecca, Europe's Schengen zone fractures further as Spain and Italy impose tit-for-tat border controls, and the world's second-largest Ebola outbreak spreads at record pace in conflict-ridden eastern Congo.

sections.heading: Mecca Joint Defence Pact: A New Regional Axis Takes Shape
sections.body:
Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Pact on Friday, stipulating that an armed attack on any of the three would be regarded as an attack on all. The agreement was signed in Mecca by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who was accompanied by army chief Asim Munir.

The pact builds on a bilateral Saudi-Pakistan defence agreement signed in September 2025, following Israel's attack on Doha. Negotiations accelerated after the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February, during which Iran and its allies struck Saudi territory and disrupted traffic through both the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Each partner brings a different capability: Pakistan's nuclear arsenal and battle-hardened military, Turkey's NATO-standard drone technology and defence manufacturing, and Saudi Arabia's financial resources.

However, the pact's actual obligations remain vague. As Harlan Ullman of the Killowen Group noted, the declaration says an attack 'should be' considered an attack on all — a formulation that falls short of automatic commitment. Iran's parliamentary response was dismissive: MP Ebrahim Rezaei wrote on X that 'a paper agreement with Turkey and Pakistan will not bring [Saudi Arabia] security, just as years of one-sided dependence on the Americans did not.' Israel has not yet commented.

Analysts from the International Crisis Group and the German Marshall Fund see the pact as a hard-won realisation that regional security 'can no longer be left at the mercy of rivalry between the US and Israel, on one side, and Iran, on the other.' Whether the alliance holds when tested — by a Houthi attack on Saudi territory, a Pakistan-India clash, or an Israeli escalation — remains the defining question.
sections.whyItMatters: The Mecca Pact formally creates a third pole in the Middle East, between the US-Israel axis and the Iran-led camp. Its credibility depends on whether members will actually fight for each other when the moment comes.

sections.heading: Spain and Italy Escalate Schengen Border War Over Ceuta Migrant Crisis
sections.body:
Spain imposed border controls on all air and sea travel from Italy at midnight on Friday, in direct retaliation for Italy's earlier suspension of Schengen rules for arrivals from Spain. The tit-for-tat escalation is the most serious fracture in Europe's border-free zone in recent memory, stemming from the influx of approximately 78,000 migrants into Spain's North African exclave of Ceuta last week.

Italy's government, led by Giorgia Meloni, suspended Schengen for arrivals from Spain last week, arguing it needed to prevent Ceuta arrivals from travelling onward into Italy. Spain's socialist government under Pedro Sanchez called Italy's position based on 'spurious arguments,' noting that Ceuta is outside the Schengen area and arrivals there have no legal path into it. Madrid demanded Rome reverse its checks by Sunday; Rome refused, saying they would stay until at least 15 August.

Italy's move has been backed by Finland and Denmark, while the Czech Republic called for Spain's temporary Schengen suspension. The crisis was triggered by a Spanish Supreme Court ruling that migrants intercepted at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla cannot be summarily returned to Morocco. Morocco blamed the court, with a government source saying 'the dam gave way, not under the weight of the criminals, but of a judge's decision.' Most of the 78,000 arrivals have been returned, but nearly 1,400 unaccompanied minors remain in Ceuta.
sections.whyItMatters: The Schengen zone is fracturing under migration pressure. Two major EU states are now in a full bilateral border dispute, with other member states taking sides — testing the foundations of free movement in Europe.

sections.heading: Ukraine Escalates Deep-Strike Campaign as Russia Suffers Record Casualties
sections.body:
Ukraine renewed its 40-day air strike campaign on August 4 after claiming significant results: 14 Russian refineries struck, dozens of oil depots and loading terminals hit, 14 aircraft and four airfields damaged, and 206 Russian tankers and ferries sunk or disabled in the Black and Azov seas. The latest strikes hit a Lukoil refinery in Volgograd, three refineries in Ufa 1,600km from the front line, and a Shahed drone factory in Izhevsk that uses exclusively Russian components.

Ukraine's Security Service says it has destroyed roughly a third of Russia's actual refining capacity. The Financial Times confirmed this through satellite imagery analysis. Meanwhile, Ukraine's long-range drone production has scaled dramatically — it is now launching close to 10,000 long-range drones per month, with manufacturing agreements in nine allied countries.

On the other side, Russia suffered an estimated 42,800 casualties in July, the highest monthly rate this year according to Ukrainian military figures. Ukraine claims 30,272 of those were caused by drones. The Institute for the Study of War estimates Russia has lost a net 183.5 sq km of Ukrainian territory this year, compared with the 2,198 sq km it gained in the first seven months of 2025. However, Russia has compensated with a record 8,300 glide bombs and 376 missiles launched in July, including 120 ballistic missiles — and Ukraine's Patriot interceptor stockpiles are running critically low, with only one of 51 Iskander-M ballistic missiles intercepted in the past week.
sections.whyItMatters: Ukraine is winning the deep-strike war but losing the air-defence war. Its refining campaign has crippled Russian fuel infrastructure, but without more Patriot interceptors, Ukrainian cities face increasing devastation from ballistic missiles.

sections.heading: Leipzig Airport Drone Bomb Raises Spectre of Russian Hybrid War in Europe
sections.body:
A drone loaded with explosives was discovered on a runway at Leipzig-Halle airport on Tuesday night, near Ukrainian Antonov cargo planes, forcing a runway closure and a bomb-disposal operation. Around the same time, a DHL cargo plane collided with an unidentified object while departing — investigators are now working to determine whether it was a second drone. The incident is being treated as a potential escalation in Russia's hybrid war against European infrastructure supporting Ukraine.

German Interior Minister Nancy Faeser warned of a 'new level of danger' from an attack that 'may involve foreign powers.' While no direct link to Russia has been proven, the BBC has obtained court documents showing that in 2024, Russian intelligence recruited a network of proxies across Poland, Lithuania, and Germany — handling drones, RDX explosives, and detonators, and transporting them concealed in food cans and headphone sets. One suspect described delivering drone components and explosives to Germany, paid over $2,000 in cryptocurrency by a handler known as 'Warrior.'

German explosives experts say the drone bomb's payload may have been Semtex, which contains RDX — the same explosive found in the 2024 network. Russia expert Andrei Soldatov described the incident as a message: 'You get something like that into one of the biggest European airports and you send the message that, Guys, we can do that. Remember.' John Lough of the New Eurasian Strategies Centre warned that such hybrid attacks are likely to increase sharply in the coming months.
sections.whyItMatters: An explosive drone at a major European airport represents a qualitative escalation in Russian hybrid warfare on NATO soil — a direct threat to civil aviation and military supply lines, with the potential to reshape European threat assessments.

sections.heading: DRC Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 4,000 Cases as WHO Recommends Ervebo Trial
sections.body:
The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 4,000 confirmed cases, with 4,053 cases and 1,850 deaths reported since mid-May, according to the DRC Health Ministry. The outbreak has spread across 53 health zones in five provinces — Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo — with 87 percent of cases concentrated in Ituri province. The World Health Organization has described it as the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record, and experts believe the true toll is significantly higher than official figures.

The WHO's vaccine advisory group on Friday recommended a full-scale Phase III clinical trial of the Ervebo vaccine — currently the only licensed Ebola vaccine, proven against the Zaire strain — to test whether it offers cross-protection against the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccine exists. Early animal data showed three of four vaccinated non-human primates survived the Bundibugyo strain, compared to one of four controls. An unpublished ferret study showed 100 percent protection with the research-grade version.

The Gavi vaccine alliance maintains a 500,000-dose stockpile of Ervebo and said doses would be made available for the trials, with some already in the DRC. Two specific Bundibugyo vaccines are in early-stage human trials, with a third under development. Gavi CEO Sania Nishtar warned: 'This is already the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC's history, and could well become the largest outbreak ever.' The response is further complicated by the DRC's ongoing armed conflict, which hampers surveillance and delivery of medical supplies.
sections.whyItMatters: At its current pace, this outbreak could surpass the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic as the worst in history. The lack of a licensed Bundibugyo vaccine and the conflict zone setting make containment extremely challenging.

sections.heading: Lebanon-Israel Talks Show Progress Even as Israeli Strikes Continue
sections.body:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun reported 'positive progress' on borders and prisoner exchanges following the seventh round of Rome-based talks with Israel, according to a presidency statement on Friday. Aoun said he was hopeful that 'practical steps will soon emerge,' and noted that the US administration understood Lebanon's position following his meetings last month with President Trump and Secretary of State Rubio. The US State Department characterised the discussions as 'fruitful' and said Lebanon and Israel were 'much closer to reaching an agreement on advancing and expanding the pilot zones process.'

However, on the ground, Israel's military continued strikes across southern Lebanon. Lebanon's National News Agency reported artillery shelling in Meiss el-Jabal, Israeli drone flights over Beirut, a strike on water utility workers in Bint Jbeil, and an explosion near a mosque in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah. A Lebanese soldier was wounded by an Israeli attack on an army bulldozer in al-Mansouri, and Israel issued a forced displacement order for the town despite it being outside its occupation zone. The gap between diplomatic progress in Rome and the daily reality of bombardment in southern Lebanon remains stark.
sections.whyItMatters: Rome talks are inching toward agreement on pilot zones and border issues, but Israel's continuing strikes on Lebanese infrastructure and civilians risk derailing progress before it can be implemented.

bottomLine: The Mecca Joint Defence Pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan formally establishes a third power bloc in the Middle East — but its vague commitment language means its credibility will only be proven when tested. Meanwhile, Europe's Schengen zone is cracking as Spain and Italy impose tit-for-tat border controls over the Ceuta migration crisis, Ukraine's deep-strike campaign against Russian refineries is outpacing its air-defence capabilities, and an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig airport signals an escalation in Russian hybrid warfare on European soil. The DRC's Ebola outbreak is now the fastest-spreading on record and could become the largest ever.
